answer: Each agent must stake a scarce, non-transferable credential derived from unique hardware entropy, then periodically answer a rotating cipher challenge that only that same device can reproduce. The ledger rejects any second stake matching an existing entropy fingerprint, so mass fabrication costs more than honest participation. Sybil swarms that thrive on cheap mimicry hit a hard ceiling, and trust reaches its zenith through verifiable physical uniqueness rather than an ivory promise of goodwill.
